_note: Per-city content for the /cities/[slug] SEO template (design/marketing/City Landing.dc.html). `cities` patches jurisdictions.City fields the canonical seeds leave blank — county on all 12, and the local prose/permit snapshot on the 11 cities seeds/content_seo.json never covered (Oakland is the design's authored example and is left untouched). `blocks.testimonials` is the per-city 'Architects licensed in {state}' line-up on scope city:<slug>; the first row also fills the hero's featured-architect card (the design derives it the same way). Names are placeholder network samples for the owner to replace as real providers go live; quote is unused by this template. The `intro` on every city is also restored here: the design moved from an escrow marketplace to an introductions platform, so each city hero now reads "Entirely remote, hired directly, stamped and permit-ready" (design/marketing/City Landing.dc.html), while seeds/cities.json still carries the superseded "escrow-backed" wording.

cities.intro: Get matched with architects licensed in Texas and fluent in Austin’s permit process — from garage-apartment ADUs to ground-up custom homes. Entirely remote, hired directly, stamped and permit-ready.
cities.body1: Austin’s Development Services Department reviews impervious cover, McMansion (Subchapter F) tent limits and heritage-tree protection alongside the building code — three constraints that decide a project long before framing does. Every architect we match is licensed in Texas and has cleared permits with the City of Austin before.
cities.body2: That local fluency shows up where it counts: cover and setback maths resolved at concept, tree and floodplain review anticipated, and drawing sets formatted for Austin’s residential intake — so you spend less time in correction cycles and more time building.
